name: ElementReliabilityDashboard

states.name: Reliability Overview Statistics
states.description: Users need summary statistics showing how many elements are stable vs flaky vs unreliable, providing a quick assessment of automation health across all tracked elements.

states.name: Elements by Reliability
states.description: Users need to see individual elements sorted by reliability, with success rates and interaction counts, to identify which specific elements need attention or alternative selectors.

states.name: Loading, Error, and Empty States

requiredElements.text: Run some automations to build up element history

states.description: Users need clear feedback during loading, error, and empty states so they understand the system status.

states.name: Reliability Color-Coded Badges
states.description: Reliability badges use color coding to quickly communicate element health: green for stable (>=95%), yellow for flaky (>=80%), red for unreliable (<80%).

states.name: Element Data Rendering
states.description: Each element row must render its element ID, total interaction count, and success rate percentage accurately from the API data. The summary cards must show correct counts of stable (>=95%), flaky (>=80%), and unreliable (<80%) elements computed from the success_rate field.

states.name: Required UI Elements
states.description: All structural elements must be present for the dashboard to function: the Shield header icon, the 3-column summary grid, the scrollable element list container, and reliability badge components.

states.name: State Transitions
states.description: The dashboard transitions cleanly between loading, error, empty, and data states. Summary card counts must be mathematically consistent with the element list (stable + flaky + unreliable = total elements).
states.precondition: Page has just loaded and is fetching from /ui-bridge/history/flaky

description: Element Reliability Dashboard — shows the stability and success rates of UI elements across automated interactions, helping users identify flaky elements that may cause automation failures.
